doc.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

title: Advice to singers sitting in
summary: Know your tune and key, interact with the band, render the lyric, and don't scat unless you have transcribed solos.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well what would you tell an aspiring singer to have ready when they go — they’re going to sit in in a club or they’re trying to get their name out there. What should they bring to the table besides —
Knowledge — know what tune they want to sing. If they’re sitting in, is that what you’re saying?

Know what tune they want to sing. Make it a tune or two or, your first objective is to, after the end of a tune would be asked to sing another. If you’re asked to sit down after the first tune you got to go back to the shed. But first of all pick a tune that plays to the strength of the band. If the band is a swinging band, you know, pick a swing tune and trade with the drummer, you know, really interact. They’re not there to back you up. Even on a gig if it’s your band, they’re not there to back you up, you’re one of the musicians. You’re part of the interplay. And also, very important, know your key. I mean I could not tell you how many times I asked the singer, “Okay, what key?” “Uh, I don’t

know.” [sings] Look at me. And I’m, you know. Yeah. So I would say that. And you know as just in terms of how you approach the music don’t sing any words longer than you say them. The rendering of a lyric to communicate with the common man, people are bombarded with all kinds of stuff. Now Frank Sinatra, you know some of my favorite singers don’t have very good voices: Frank Sinatra, Tony Bennett. They didn’t have great voices. But they knew how to render a lyric. And you know that concept is like when you cook a piece of meat you’re rendering the fat. When you render a lyric you’re excising the meaning out of every syllable. That’s what rendering a lyric is. And you’re telling a story. So don’t be so in your head that you’re concentrating on how you sound and by all means don’t scat unless you’ve transcribed solos. Because singers, many singers, and some, many great singers think they can scat [scats] and it’s all bullshit. You know there’s a singer in Manhattan named Veronica Swift. She is the next big thing. She’s transcribed Freddie, you can, I mean she’s deep, deep, deep. So don’t scat. Because it’s been done so well already that unless you’re good you’re going to get exposed.
Wow. Great answers. I was watching you play.
